title: Versioning Prompts and Catching Regressions
summary: A prompt is code that nobody can read the behaviour of by inspection. This lesson treats prompts as versioned artifacts and builds the testing machinery around them: golden sets, confidence intervals on pass rates, significance tests between versions, and release gates that do not cry wolf.
objectives: Manage prompts as versioned, reviewable artifacts with changelogs, pinned model versions and rollback
Size a golden set and compute a confidence interval for a measured pass rate
Compare two prompt versions with a two-proportion test, a paired test, and a power calculation
Explain why flaky cases and multiple comparisons produce false alarms, and set a release gate that accounts for them
Turn production failures into new regression cases
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with probability of independent events from earlier lessons in this module and with the idea of a pass rate. A little statistics (a proportion, a standard error) helps but is explained as we go. Evaluation proper is the subject of module 5; here we use just what prompt changes need.
